sanskrit: yac ca varcaḥ kanyāsu yac ca hastiṣv āhitam | hiraṇye goṣu yad varcas tasya bhakṣīya varcasaḥ ||
english: Whatever radiance is lodged in maidens, whatever is lodged in elephants, whatever radiance abides in gold and in cattle — of that radiance may I partake.

sanskrit: yac ca varco rājarathe yac ca rājasv āhitam | niṣke rukme ca yad varcas tasya bhakṣīya varcasaḥ ||
english: Whatever radiance is in the royal chariot, whatever is lodged in kings, whatever radiance abides in the niṣka-ornament and in gold — of that radiance may I partake.

sanskrit: yad apsu yad vanaspatau yad agnau yac ca sūrye | yajñe dakṣiṇāyāṃ varcas tasya bhakṣīya varcasaḥ ||
english: Whatever radiance is in the waters, whatever in the forest-lord, whatever in Agni and in the Sun, whatever radiance abides in the sacrifice and in the sacrificial fee — of that radiance may I partake.

sanskrit: varcasvan me mukham astu varcasvad uta me śiraḥ | varcasvān viśvataḥ pratyaṅ varcasvān varṇo astu me ||
english: May my face be full of radiance, and my head too be radiant; may I be radiant on all sides — may my complexion be radiant.

sanskrit: subhāgaṃ me mukham astu subhāgam uta me śiraḥ | subhāgo viśvataḥ pratyaṅ subhāgo varṇo astu me ||
english: May my face be auspicious, and my head too be auspicious; may I be auspicious on all sides — may my complexion be auspicious.

sanskrit: ud asau sūryo agāt saha vahatunā mama | ahaṃ te madhumatī madhughān madhumattarā ||
english: Yonder Sun has risen together with my bridal procession. I am honeyed for you, honey-producing, yet more honey-sweet.

sanskrit: yad giriṣu parvateṣu goṣv aśveṣu yan madhu | surāyāṃ sicyamānāyāṃ kīlāle madhu tan mayi ||
english: Whatever honey is in the mountains and on the highland peaks, in cattle and in horses, the honey in surā as it is poured, the honey in kīlāla — let all that be in me.

sanskrit: yathā surā yathā madhu yathākṣā adhidevane | yathā ha gavyato mana evā mām abhi te manaḥ ||
english: As surā, as honey, as the dice upon the gaming board, as the mind of one enamoured of cattle — even so may your mind be fixed upon me.

sanskrit: ā te padaṃ padenādiṣy ā te manasā manaḥ | pratyañcam agrabhaṃ tvā- -aśvam ivāśvābhidhānyā ||
english: I have trodden upon your footstep with my foot; I have drawn your mind to me with my mind. I have seized you who face me, as a mare is haltered with a horse-tether.

sanskrit: mahyaṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī mahyaṃ devī sarasvatī | mahyaṃ tvā madhyaṃ bhūmyā ubhāv antau sam asyatām ||
english: Heaven and Earth have joined you to me; the goddess Sarasvatī has joined you to me; for me may both ends of the earth's middle be yoked together for you.

sanskrit: yā vaiśvadevīr iṣavo yā vasūnāṃ yā rudrasya somasya yā bhagasya | viśve devā iṣavo yāvatīr vas tā vo agninā śarmaṇā śamayāmi ||
english: The arrows that belong to all the gods, those of the Vasus, those of Rudra, of Soma, and of Bhaga — all you gods, however many your arrows may be, those I appease with the protection of Agni.

sanskrit: yā ādityānām iṣavo yā vasūnāṃ yā rudrasyāśvinor yāvatīs tāḥ | viśve devā iṣavo yāvatīr vas tā vo devaḥ savitā śamayāti ||
english: The arrows of the Ādityas, those of the Vasus, those of Rudra and of the Aśvins, however many they are — all you gods, however many your arrows, the god Savitā shall appease them.

sanskrit: yās te agna iṣavo vāta yās te apām adityām uta yā marutsu | indraś ca sāmnā varuṇaś ca rājā tā vaḥ sūryo bṛhatā śamayāti ||
english: Your arrows, O Agni, your arrows, O Vāta, those of the waters and of Aditi, and those among the Maruts — Indra with his pacifying chant and king Varuṇa, and the Sun with his greatness shall appease them.

sanskrit: mā vṛkṣmahy ādityebhyo mā vasubhyo mā rudrāyāgnaye pārthivāya | indrasya śuco varuṇasya yāḥ śucas tā vo devy aditiḥ śamayāti ||
english: May we not be smitten by the Ādityas, nor by the Vasus, nor by Rudra, nor by the earthly Agni. The scorchings of Indra and the scorchings of Varuṇa — the goddess Aditi shall appease those of yours.

sanskrit: yāś ca vāte viṣvagvāte yāś ca rudrasya dhanvani | agniṣ ṭā vasor īśānaḥ sarvās tā bheṣajā karat ||
english: Those arrows that are in the wind, in the all-pervading wind, and those that are in Rudra's quiver — may Agni, the lord of the Vasu, make all of them remedies.
